hazard: Absence of timely debrief after incident

reports.title: Freeda Glausiusz: Prevention of future deaths report

promises.quote: In May 2020, immediately, after Ms [name redacted] death, the Deputy Borough Director listened to calls by each staff member to assess the quality of the care being provided.
promises.summary: Monthly supervision of Crisis Line calls by senior staff

promises.quote: In July 2021, the Deputy Borough Director listened to recorded calls from each staff member working on the Crisis Line. The standard was overall good. However, the outcome was that the contract of an Agency Nurse was terminated and another nurse was commenced on a performance management process.
promises.summary: Termination of agency nurse and performance management

promises.quote: Between 20 November 2021 - 28 November 2021, the CCG conducted a 'mystery shopping' audit of the Crisis line to measure responsiveness to calls. 70% of calls were answered in one minute or less, with 20% less than two minutes.
promises.summary: Mystery shopping audit of Crisis Line responsiveness

promises.quote: From January 2022, a larger Trust-wide Crisis Line call quality audit will take place. The audit tool has already been devised.
promises.summary: Trust-wide Crisis Line call quality audit

promises.quote: The City and Hackney Crisis Line Operational Policy has been updated to include a section on how call handlers should deal with concerned relatives and family members. This will be ratified on 17th December at the ELFT London Crisis Strategy Group and the updated content will be discussed with staff members at their team business meeting on 6 January 2022.
promises.summary: Policy update on handling concerned relatives

promises.quote: medical records training for all senior nurses was provided on 24 November 2021 to all senior nurses and managers at the Trust. The focus of the training was good record keeping, observations and retrospective record keeping.
promises.summary: Medical records training for senior nurses

concerns.quote: I was shocked when I listened to the recording of the call that [REDACTED] made to the crisis line the day before his daughter died.
concerns.hazard: lack of seriousness in crisis line calls

concerns.quote: The East London NHS Foundation Trust (ELFT) serious incident (SI) report observed that the clinician did not elicit clear risks during the conversation; did not listen to [REDACTED] ; talked over him; did not appear empathic; and dismissed his distress about his daughter, even though she was a patient known to services after a first episode of psychosis.
concerns.hazard: failure to assess and respond to risk

concerns.quote: This is not the first time that I have made a PFD report to ELFT about its crisis line.
concerns.hazard: repeated failure to act on prior concerns

concerns.quote: I received a copy of the SI report the day before the inquest.
concerns.hazard: delayed provision of internal investigation documents

concerns.quote: I never received a copy of the 48 hour hot de-brief.
concerns.hazard: absence of timely debrief after incident

concerns.quote: My officer first requested witness statements and a copy of any internal investigation on 7 June, over four months ago, and asked for the statements to be provided by 20 August.
concerns.hazard: unreasonable delay in providing witness statements

reports.title: Andrew Largin: Prevention of future deaths report

concerns.quote: The ELFT serious incident (SI) review report identified that, although Mr Largin was discharged to the Woodberry Wetlands neighbourhood rehabilitation team from the crisis (i.e. home treatment) team on 25 January 2022, the neighbourhood team did not allocate him to a team member until 3 February
concerns.hazard: lack of timely allocation to a team member

concerns.quote: the crisis team failed to reassess him or to re-open his case to the crisis team, but instead referred the community team to the neighbourhood team
concerns.hazard: failure to reassess and reopen case

concerns.quote: the crisis team member who made the decision on 2 February simply to advise that Mr Largin should be dealt with by the neighbourhood team failed to record any reasons for her decision
concerns.hazard: lack of documented rationale for decision

concerns.quote: the SI reviewing team had not even spoken to that crisis team member as part of their investigation, let alone fed back to her
there was a hot de-brief after Mr [name redacted] death. However, no notes were made of that and no entry was made on Mr [name redacted] medical record

the crisis team and the neighbourhood team did not share an understanding of how quickly the neighbourhood team aims to make contact with patients, to assist in their decision making about the correct pathway for a patient

links.explanation: Both reports highlight that a hot debrief following a death was not properly documented or shared. The earlier case notes the missing copy of the 48‑hour hot debrief, while the later case notes that although a hot debrief occurred, no notes or medical record entry were made.
links.earlier_quote: I never received a copy of the 48 hour hot de-brief.
links.later_quote: However, no notes were made of that and no entry was made on Mr [name redacted] medical record
